items.title: OPTI-AML: prospective comparison of 28 vs 14 days of venetoclax induction with azacitidine in older adults with AML
items.abstract: Prospective randomized phase 2 OPTI-AML trial comparing 28-day versus abbreviated 14-day venetoclax dosing with azacitidine for cycles 1-2 in genomically unselected older/unfit newly diagnosed AML, testing whether shorter venetoclax reduces prolonged cytopenias while preserving efficacy.

items.title: Regional practice differences significantly impact benefit from post-HCT gilteritinib for FLT3-ITD AML
items.abstract: Post-hoc analysis of the phase 3 BMT CTN 1506 (MORPHO) trial showing the survival benefit of post-transplant gilteritinib maintenance in FLT3-ITD AML is concentrated in patients transplanted sooner after diagnosis and those with detectable pre-HCT FLT3-ITD MRD, explaining the North America versus Europe/Asia discrepancy.

items.title: Clinical and genomic convergence of high-risk CCUS and lower-risk myelodysplastic syndromes/neoplasms
items.abstract: Prospective study of 409 patients with clonal cytopenia of undetermined significance (CCUS) and 241 with lower-risk MDS applying harmonized criteria and the CHRS/CCRS risk scores, showing high-risk CCUS behaves clinically and genomically like lower-risk MDS and may warrant trial enrollment.

items.title: Non-invasive multiparametric characterization of essential thrombocythemia, prefibrotic and overt myelofibrosis
items.abstract: Prospective study of 128 patients (44 ET, 53 prefibrotic MF, 21 overt MF) evaluating non-invasive parameters to distinguish these MPN subtypes, showing the mutational landscape grows increasingly complex from ET to prefibrotic to overt myelofibrosis and identifying differentially expressed markers that could reduce reliance on marrow biopsy.

items.title: SLF2 and SMC5 dysfunction drives HSC aging and predisposes to MDS, defining a new inherited bone marrow failure syndrome
items.abstract: Mechanistic study of Atelis Syndrome (pathogenic SLF2/SMC5 variants) showing the resulting hematopoietic progenitor defects drive stem-cell aging and early-onset MDS, establishing SLF2/SMC5 dysfunction as a new inherited bone marrow failure syndrome with leukemia predisposition.

items.title: Glofitamab plus gemcitabine and oxaliplatin for relapsed/refractory DLBCL: 3-year follow-up of STARGLO
items.abstract: Three-year follow-up of the phase 3 STARGLO trial in transplant-ineligible relapsed/refractory DLBCL, where glofitamab plus GemOx maintained superior overall survival versus rituximab-GemOx (median OS 25.5 vs 12.5 months; HR 0.60) with durable responses across clinically relevant subgroups.

items.title: Large B-cell lymphoma after CD19 CAR-T failure: updated real-world outcomes, prognostic factors, and prediction models
items.abstract: Single-center retrospective cohort of large B-cell lymphoma patients who relapsed or progressed after CD19 CAR-T, developing clinical prediction models for survival after subsequent therapy in a setting where outcomes remain poor and prognostic tools are lacking.

items.title: Haematopoietic cell transplantation for relapsed or refractory classical Hodgkin lymphoma: an EBMT registry cohort of 19 498 patients
items.abstract: Retrospective EBMT Lymphoma Working Group registry study of 19,498 autologous and allogeneic transplants for relapsed/refractory classical Hodgkin lymphoma from 2010-2022, evaluating how novel agents, donor selection and GVHD prophylaxis have changed post-transplant outcomes.

items.title: Talquetamab in relapsed/refractory multiple myeloma: 3-year follow-up of the phase 1/2 MonumenTAL-1 study
items.abstract: Three-year follow-up of MonumenTAL-1 for the GPRC5D-directed bispecific talquetamab in relapsed/refractory myeloma, reporting overall response rates of 67-74% in T-cell-redirection-naive cohorts with durable responses and characterizing the distinctive skin, nail and oral GPRC5D-related toxicities over long-term dosing.

items.title: De-escalation trials in multiple myeloma: past, present and future
items.abstract: Review synthesizing emerging de-escalation strategies in multiple myeloma - dose/schedule modification, agent withdrawal, fixed-duration therapy with treatment-free intervals, MRD-adapted approaches, ASCT omission and single CAR-T infusion - as increasingly effective immunotherapies move earlier and the field asks how much therapy is needed to sustain response.

items.title: Targeting BCMA in patients with relapsed/refractory multiple myeloma in 1 to 3 prior lines of therapy
items.abstract: Practical review synthesizing the recent wave of phase 3 BCMA-directed CAR T-cell, bispecific-antibody and antibody-drug-conjugate data in early-relapse (1-3 prior lines) myeloma, comparing trial populations and framing treatment-selection and sequencing decisions.

items.title: Measurable residual disease-dependent unfavorable outcomes in pediatric PAX5-rearranged B-acute lymphoblastic leukemia
items.abstract: Analysis of 159 pediatric PAX5-rearranged B-ALL cases treated within AIEOP-BFM ALL studies across Italy, Germany and Austria, revealing high-risk clinical features and higher relapse rates versus non-PAX5-r ALL, with MRD identifying the patients at greatest risk of unfavorable outcome.

items.title: Lisocabtagene maraleucel combined with ibrutinib in R/R CLL or SLL: primary results from TRANSCEND CLL 004
items.abstract: Primary results of the liso-cel plus concurrent ibrutinib cohort of the phase 1/2 TRANSCEND CLL 004 study in relapsed/refractory CLL/SLL, reporting complete-response rates and safety for combining CD19 CAR T cells with continuous BTK inhibition.

items.title: Cytokine release syndrome and ICANS following axicabtagene ciloleucel or brexucabtagene autoleucel CAR T-cell therapy: CIBMTR data
items.abstract: Real-world CIBMTR registry analysis quantifying the incidence, severity and management of cytokine release syndrome and immune effector cell-associated neurotoxicity syndrome (ICANS) after axi-cel or brexu-cel across approved B-cell malignancy indications.

items.title: Early neurologic response predicts outcomes after anakinra for immune effector cell-associated neurotoxicity syndrome
items.abstract: Analysis of 101 patients treated with the IL-1 receptor antagonist anakinra for ICANS (90 corticosteroid-refractory) after CAR T-cell therapy, showing median time to ICANS resolution of 8 days and that early neurologic response predicts recovery, helping guide use of anakinra in severe neurotoxicity.

items.title: Low-dose ruxolitinib for graft-versus-host disease prevention in haploidentical stem-cell transplantation: a phase 3 trial
items.abstract: Multicentre, open-label, randomised phase 3 trial testing whether replacing mycophenolate mofetil with low-dose ruxolitinib within an ATG/calcineurin-inhibitor/methotrexate backbone reduces acute GVHD after haploidentical HSCT, extending JAK1/2 inhibition from steroid-refractory treatment into prophylaxis.

items.title: Characteristics of donor and recipient clonal hematopoiesis in nonmyeloablative transplant for sickle cell disease
items.abstract: Study characterizing donor- and recipient-derived clonal hematopoiesis in patients undergoing nonmyeloablative allogeneic transplant for sickle cell disease, addressing concern that curative cellular therapies could raise the risk of therapy-related MDS/AML.

items.title: Renin-angiotensin-aldosterone system inhibition exacerbates anemia in sickle cell disease
items.abstract: Multicenter analysis combining a 658-patient Walk-PHaSST cross-sectional cohort, two longitudinal cohorts and a mouse model showing that renin-angiotensin-aldosterone system inhibitors - often used for albuminuria in sickle cell disease - independently lower hemoglobin and reduce erythroid colony formation, warranting close hemoglobin monitoring.

items.title: Platelet-activating anti-platelet factor 4 disorders
items.abstract: Review of the platelet-activating anti-PF4 disorders spectrum, spanning classic heparin-induced thrombocytopenia, autoimmune and spontaneous HIT variants, and vaccine-induced immune thrombotic thrombocytopenia (VITT), detailing their distinct antibody behaviors and highly prothrombotic clinical features.

items.title: Better 10-year cerebrovascular outcome after transplant than standard care in sickle cell anemia: DREPAGREFFE-2 trial
items.abstract: Ten-year follow-up of the French multicenter DREPAGREFFE trial comparing matched-sibling-donor transplant with standard care in 67 children with sickle cell anemia and cerebral vasculopathy; transplant yielded no deaths or strokes, better quality of life, fewer hospitalizations, and significantly improved stenosis, silent-infarct and cognitive scores, supporting earlier transplant.

items.title: Contemporary management of pediatric venous thrombosis: how does it differ from adult care?
items.abstract: JTH in Clinic review contrasting pediatric and adult venous thromboembolism management, covering the expanding but still-selective use of direct oral anticoagulants in children, the ongoing role of low-molecular-weight and unfractionated heparin, shorter treatment durations for provoked events, and the value of pediatric anticoagulation stewardship.

items.title: Intravesical cretostimogene grenadenorepvec oncolytic immunotherapy in BCG-unresponsive NMIBC with carcinoma in situ (BOND-003 Cohort C)
items.abstract: Single-arm phase 3 BOND-003 Cohort C trial of the oncolytic immunotherapy cretostimogene grenadenorepvec in high-risk, BCG-unresponsive non-muscle-invasive bladder cancer with carcinoma in situ, offering a bladder-sparing option with a manageable adverse-event profile.

items.title: Clinical toxicity of ADCs and ICI-ADC combinations: mechanisms, patterns and management
items.abstract: Review proposing a unified, mechanism-informed framework for the overlapping pulmonary, hepatic, gastrointestinal and cutaneous toxicities of antibody-drug conjugates and ICI-ADC combinations, with practical algorithms for evaluation, management and rechallenge as these combinations move into earlier, curative-intent settings.

items.title: Local management of second ipsilateral breast cancer events after primary breast-conserving therapy: an international Delphi consensus
items.abstract: International Delphi consensus of 36 surgical and radiation oncology experts reaching agreement on 80% of items for managing second ipsilateral breast cancer events, endorsing repeat breast-conserving therapy for selected patients and defining suitability criteria including inter-surgery interval, molecular profile and prior toxicity.

items.title: AI-based augmentation of oncology clinical trials
items.abstract: Review of artificial-intelligence applications across the oncology clinical-trial lifecycle, arguing the most immediate evidence-supported role is augmenting operational workflows under human oversight - patient identification, eligibility assessment, data extraction and monitoring - while synthetic control arms and digital twins remain early and unvalidated.

items.title: Decade-long persistence of CD19 CAR T cells in B cell lymphomas
items.abstract: Study characterizing the extent and biology of long-term persistence of 4-1BB-costimulated anti-CD19 CAR T cells (CART19) in B-cell lymphoma patients, documenting detectable CAR T cells up to a decade after infusion and profiling the phenotype of these ultra-long-lived cells.

items.title: Latent effector T cells mediate immunotherapy responses in the bone marrow microenvironment
items.abstract: Integrating TCR profiling, HLA immunopeptidomics and functional screening in multiple myeloma and AML, this study defines a latent but activatable tumor-reactive T-cell program in bone marrow distinct from solid-tumor exhaustion, and builds a transcriptional classifier (TFiT) that stratifies immunotherapy - but not chemotherapy - response.

items.title: Beyond BCL-2: what drives venetoclax resistance in acute myeloid leukemia?
items.abstract: Review mapping the increasingly defined mechanisms of venetoclax resistance in AML - compensatory or lineage-associated switches toward MCL-1 or BCL-xL dependence, oncogenic signaling, differentiation state, emerging BAX mutations and metabolic adaptations sustaining oxidative phosphorylation - and their implications for combination strategies.

items.title: Teclistamab in multiple myeloma with one to three previous lines of therapy (MajesTEC-9)
items.abstract: Phase 3 MajesTEC-9 trial randomizing 593 patients with relapsed/refractory myeloma after 1-3 prior lines to the BCMAxCD3 bispecific teclistamab versus PVd or Kd; teclistamab significantly improved progression-free (18-month 69.8% vs 26.9%) and overall survival, moving bispecifics into earlier relapse despite grade 3/4 infections in 41.6%.
